name: File Hash / Checksum Verifier
description: Compute the SHA-256 checksum of any file in your browser and compare it against the hash provided by the download source.
body:
🔐

Drop a file here or click to browse

SHA-256 computed locally via Web Crypto

Hashing…

Result

Drop a file to compute and verify its hash.
howto: Copy the SHA-256 hash shown on the page you downloaded the file from.
Paste it into the Expected hash field.
Drop the downloaded file onto the dropzone.
The tool computes the file's real SHA-256 and compares them.
A match confirms the download is intact; a mismatch means the file is corrupt or tampered with — download it again.
features: Live match / mismatch result with color coding
Handles hashes pasted with or without a sha256: prefix

faq.q: Why should I verify a file hash?
faq.a: Downloads can be corrupted mid-transfer or tampered with. Verifying the SHA-256 hash against the one published by the source proves the file is byte-for-byte what was published.

faq.q: What if the hash doesn't match?
faq.a: Do not trust the file. Re-download it, ideally over HTTPS, and verify again. A persistent mismatch may mean the file is corrupt or came from an untrusted source.

faq.q: Can I verify MD5 or SHA-1 here?
faq.a: This tool computes SHA-256, which is the modern standard. MD5 and SHA-1 are considered weak and are rarely published anymore.
Yes. Hashing runs locally using your browser's built-in Web Crypto implementation — the file never leaves your machine.
